paper.title_en: Resolving the Quantum Origin of Anisotropic Raman Response in Quasi-1D $Ta_2$$Ni_3$$Te_5$
paper.abstract_en: Probing anisotropic electron-phonon interactions (EPIs) is fundamental to understanding low-dimensional quantum materials, yet isolating their intrinsic signatures remains a challenge due to the confounding influence of extrinsic effects. Here, we resolve this ambiguity in quasi-one-dimensional $Ta_2$$Ni_3$$Te_5$ through a combination of angle-resolved polarized Raman spectroscopy and density functional perturbation theory (DFPT). Anomalous four-lobe angular dependences were observed in Ag phonon modes, which deviate from the real-valued Raman tensor prediction. Further, we explicitly highlight that, despite their distinct physical origins, light absorption and birefringence yield mathematically identical angular dependencies in $Ta_2$$Ni_3$$Te_5$, rendering phenomenological fitting alone insufficient to identify the true physical mechanism. By employing a full quantum treatment incorporating detailed interaction mechanisms, we capture the qualitative characteristics and mode-to-mode diversity of the anomalous angular responses observed experimentally. The DFPT calculations further reveal mode-specific and momentum-resolved EPIs, providing microscopic support for anisotropic EPIs as the mechanism of anomalous Raman responses.
